text_excerpt: NFFA-Europe  Metadata Template Detailed metadata are essential for ensuring data quality control, facilitating efficient dataset storage and retrieval, and enabling both primary and secondary users to effectively reuse the data.  NFFA-Europe  requires thorough documentation to support the long-term maintenance and distribution of study datasets. NFFA-Europe  Metadata Components The metadata should include the following details: Study Purpose  – A brief description of why the study was conducted. Partners and People involved  – A list of individuals involved in various aspects of the study, including design, data collection, analysis, and data management. Study Methods  – A detailed explanation of the methodologies used, ensuring that secondary users can understand the process without needing to contact the principal investigator. Variable Details  – Comprehensive descriptions of each variable included in the dataset. Data file and variable names should be concise yet descriptive, clearly reflecting the content of the file. Experimental data should be stored in CSV format. If initially working in an Excel spreadsheet, ensure that it does not contain formulas or cell comments. If comments are necessary, include them in separate columns labeled, for example, ' field_notes ' or 'comments'. If the data were originally used in a database and require significant table linking for analysis, normalize them into flat files instead of simply exporting database tables. Short name or nickname you use to refer to this dataset- File naming convention (FNC): Data 27042026 _ Characterization _ AFM_CA_Biointerfaces_Figure2 _ FORTH Metadata 27042026 _Characterization_AFM_CA_Biointerfaces_Figure2_FORTH_README * BRIEF NAME should be clear and relevant, helping to identify the content Abstract This dataset was generated as part of NFFA-Europe/FORTH activities to support the physicochemical and surface-mechanical characterization of cellulose acetate (CA)  biointerfaces  developed for mesenchymal stem cell response and osteogenic commitment studies. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurements were performed on CA replicas with three different surface topographies: Flat, Low Roughness (LR), and High Roughness (HR). The measurements were used to evaluate surface morphology, topographical features, local stiffness, adhesion, and reduced Young’s modulus of the CA  biointerfaces . The dataset includes AFM topographic images, phase/topography-related outputs, nanomechanical maps, force-distance curve data, and derived image files corresponding to the Flat, Low Roughness, and High Roughness CA samples. These data support the AFM-based analysis presented in the article “ Microstructured  cellulose acetate  biointerfaces  regulate mesenchymal stem cell response and promote osteogenic commitment”, specifically the AFM characterization and Figure 2. The CA replicas were fabricated using soft lithography from PDMS negative molds, reproducing the surface morphology of laser- microstructured  silicon master substrates. 2D topographic images, phase images, nanomechanical maps, and force-distance curves were acquired using a Dimension Icon Atomic Force Microscope equipped with a  Nanoscope  V controller (Bruker, Billerica, MA, USA). Measurements were conducted in  PeakForce  mode. Scan ranges varied from 50 µm to 0.5 µm, with typical adjusted scan rates of 0.2–1 Hz. Image resolution ranged from 256 × 256 pixels to 512 × 512 pixels. RTESPA-300 etched silicon probes with reflective Al coating and nominal resonance frequency of 300 kHz were used.
